biography: Conner Grady, a name synonymous with calculated risk in the British GT scene, hails from a small village nestled in the Cotswolds. His journey began not on the asphalt, but on the muddy fields of his family's farm, where he honed his reflexes dodging tractors and navigating treacherous terrain on an old motorbike. He transitioned to karting at 16, quickly making a name for himself with his uncanny ability to dissect a track and exploit every inch. A defining moment came at the Brands Hatch Ginetta GT4 Supercup in 2008, where, starting from the back of the grid due to a mechanical failure, he clawed his way to a stunning victory, showcasing his tenacity and tactical brilliance. Now a seasoned veteran with Ginetta, Grady remains a formidable competitor, respected for his consistency and ability to extract the maximum from his machinery. While a championship has eluded him, his dedication and shrewd racecraft ensure he's always a threat.
drivingStyle: Grady's driving style is best described as clinical. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes or aggressive corner entries. Instead, he prioritizes precision and consistency, meticulously building speed throughout a race. He's a master of tire management, nursing his rubber through long stints while maintaining a relentless pace. Under pressure, Grady remains remarkably composed, rarely making mistakes and capitalizing on the errors of others. His approach is less about raw speed and more about strategic execution, making him a formidable opponent in endurance races.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2012 Spa 24 Hours in the Ginetta G55 GT4, a grueling endurance race that tested his mental and physical limits.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out on the first lap of the 2018 British GT Championship finale at Donington Park due to a mechanical failure, ending his hopes of a championship title.
